decisions.reason: The call at cp 9126 is identical to an earlier call (locked u2). Guide 3.2 states that 'identical short-footnote calls bind to the first such call', i.e. the definition MediaWiki uses for a repeated identical {sfn} is the first call, whereas a content-bearing <ref> is stated to be 'its own definition'. The guide singles out repeated identical sfn calls to bind elsewhere, so a repeated call is a use of the first call's definition, not a definition of its own. The raw HTML agrees: every call renders a <sup> with data-mw name 'FOOTNOTEThiollay1994' and body pointing to the single list item cite_note-FOOTNOTEThiollay1994-11; there is one rendered footnote, not several. The locked label already has this call as a use bound to the first identical call {{sfn|Thiollay|1994}} at cp 5814 (locked d1, in_window false). Ambiguity: 3.1 lists 'a short-footnote template call' among content-carrying references, which read alone could make every call a definition. But that reading conflicts with the explicit 3.2 binding rule, and 3.1 itself merges same-name definitions into 'one reference'. The reading that follows both sections is the locked one: one definition at the first identical call.
